files.purpose: Wraps UsagePanel in a draggable, dismissible floating glass panel that sits across the column from the Hydra heads (left by default), sized by the placer to the content height it reports back, with a top strip that acts as the drag handle and carries the title and close button.
calls_into: WindowBackdrop (named in a comment only, as the precedent for letting glass supply the edge)
state_owned: No @State of its own: the panel is entirely driven by its let properties and callback closures
side_effects: Calls onContentHeight(_:) from .onGeometryChange whenever the scrolled content height changes, passing measured height + HydraPanel.stripHeight + 8
Calls onContentHeight(HydraPanel.stripHeight + 44) once from .onAppear in the empty state
Calls onDrag(CGSize) / onDragEnd() from the two PanelDragHandle instances while the handle is dragged
Calls dismiss() from the xmark ChromeCircleButton
No file, network, process, keychain or timer work of its own
platform_assumptions: glassEffect(.regular, in: shape) is the macOS 26 Liquid Glass modifier
SF Symbol "xmark" for the close button
Drop shadow and live-resize tracking assume an AppKit-hosted SwiftUI window exposing WindowLiveResize
persisted_fields: None. This view persists nothing; panel geometry and position are supplied by the caller through size, onDrag and onContentHeight.
ui_elements: Panel shape: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: HydraPanel.cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
Content: ScrollView(.vertical) containing UsagePanel(usage:provider:headsProvider:fillsWidth: true)
Content insets: .padding(.top, HydraPanel.stripHeight) and .padding(.bottom, 8)
Reported content height: measured height + HydraPanel.stripHeight + 8

Empty state text (verbatim, interpolated): "Nothing to show for \(provider.displayName) yet." at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.secondaryText, padded .top by HydraPanel.stripHeight, .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
Empty state reports a fixed content height of HydraPanel.stripHeight + 44
Outer frame: .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
.animation(nil, value: liveResize.isActive) so the frame follows the pane every frame of a live resize
Glass background: shape.fill(.clear).glassEffect(.regular, in: shape) overlaid with shape.fill(Chrome.glassTint.opacity(isDark ? 0.22 : 0.16))
.clipShape(shape) with no hairline stroke (comment: glass supplies the edge, a hairline read as a second ring when the window was key)
Scrim background under the glass: shape.fill((isDark ? Color.black : Color.white).opacity(isDark ? 0.3 : 0.34)) with .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isDark ? 1 : 0.65), radius: 28, y: 10)
Strip: HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 8) applied as .overlay(alignment: .top)

Title capsule: HStack(spacing: 6) with ProviderIcon(provider: provider, size: 12), an optional second ProviderIcon(provider: headsProvider, size: 12), then Text("Usage") at .font(.system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium)) in Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.92)

Title capsule chrome: .padding(.horizontal, Chrome.capsuleHorizontalPadding), .frame(height: Chrome.capsuleContentHeight), .padding(.vertical, Chrome.capsuleVerticalPadding), .fixedSize(), .chromeGlassCapsule()
Title capsule overlaid with a PanelDragHandle so the label drags the panel too; .padding(.top, Chrome.chromeTopPadding), .padding(.leading, Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding)
Middle PanelDragHandle: .frame(maxWidth: .infinity), .frame(height: HydraPanel.stripHeight), .help("Drag to move"), .accessibilityLabel(Text("Drag to move"))

Close button: ChromeCircleButton(symbol: "xmark", help: "Dismiss the usage panel; the usage popover opens it again"), .padding(.top, Chrome.chromeTopPadding), .padding(.trailing, Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding)
feature_notes: hasSomething gate: the scrolling content shows when usage?.fraction != nil OR PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits(provider) OR CreditsReader.exposesCredits(provider) OR headsProvider.map { exposesLimits || exposesCredits } == true; otherwise the placeholder "Nothing to show for <Provider> yet." shows

The heads provider's icon appears beside the lead's in the title capsule whenever headsProvider is non-nil; unlike UsagePanel, the strip does not additionally test headsProvider != provider, so an identical heads provider would draw a duplicate icon here
Closing is reversible and the help text says so: the usage popover opens the panel again
Panel visual recipe is exactly three layers: a scrim carrying the single shadow (radius 28, y 10), the glass, and the theme tint overlay
Dark mode differences: tint opacity 0.22 vs 0.16 light, scrim black 0.3 vs white 0.34, shadow opacity 1 vs 0.65
unresolved_questions: HydraPanel.cornerRadius and HydraPanel.stripHeight literal point values are defined outside this file
Chrome.capsuleHorizontalPadding, capsuleContentHeight, capsuleVerticalPadding, chromeTopPadding and chromeHorizontalPadding literals live in the Chrome namespace, not here
Which view computes and applies `size` and the drag offsets (the 'placer' named in the doc comment) is not in this file
No #available gate for .glassEffect appears here, so whether availability is handled upstream is not determinable from this file

files.purpose: Composes one chat's usage readout: the context-window row plus bar, then the provider's plan limits and credits, stacking the Hydra lead's and heads' providers as two labelled sections when a pair sends its heads out on a different provider. Used both in the composer popover at a fixed 360 points and inside UsageFloatingPanel with fillsWidth.
key_symbols: UsagePanel.init(usage:provider:headsProvider:fillsWidth:) with defaults headsProvider: nil, fillsWidth: false
private @ViewBuilder func providerSection(_ p: ProviderKind, role: String, needsDivider: Bool) -> some View
static func tokens(_ count: Int) -> String
nested local func compact(_ value: Double, _ suffix: String) -> String
state_owned: No @State: the view is a pure function of its inputs plus the registry
side_effects: .onAppear calls registry.refreshPlanLimits(provider) and registry.refreshCredits(provider), and the same pair for the heads provider when one applies
These are the only refresh triggers in the usage stack: PlanLimitsView and CreditsView only render
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI on macOS with the Observation @Environment(Type.self) form
String(format: "%.1f", value) uses Foundation/ICU locale-sensitive formatting
persisted_fields: None. Nothing is written to UserDefaults or disk here; plan limits and credits are read from the in-memory ProviderRegistry.
ui_elements: Root: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0)

Context row: HStack with Text("Context window") in Chrome.secondaryText, Spacer(minLength: 12), then Text(verbatim: "\(Self.tokens(usage.usedTokens)) / \(Self.tokens(window)) (\(Int((fraction * 100).rounded()))%)") in Chrome.secondaryText with .monospacedDigit()
Context row font applied to the whole HStack: .font(.system(size: 13))
Context bar: UsageBar(fraction: fraction, tint: Chrome.accent, label: "Context window") with .padding(.top, 10)
Divider().padding(.vertical, 14) before PlanLimitsView and before CreditsView in the single-provider path, only when showsContext
Hydra path: providerSection(provider, role: "Lead", needsDivider: showsContext) then providerSection(heads, role: "Heads", needsDivider: showsContext || showsLimits || showsCredits)

Section header: HStack(spacing: 6) with ProviderIcon(provider: p, size: 13) and Text(verbatim: "\(role) · \(p.displayName)") at .font(.system(size: 12, weight: .semibold)) in Chrome.primaryText, then .padding(.bottom, 8)
Inside a section, Divider().padding(.vertical, 14) separates PlanLimitsView from CreditsView when both show
Outer padding: .padding(16)
Width: .frame(width: fillsWidth ? nil : 360) plus .frame(maxWidth: fillsWidth ? .infinity : nil, alignment: .leading)
feature_notes: Popover width is exactly 360 points; the floating-panel variant passes fillsWidth: true and takes the panel's width, left-aligned
The heads section is only drawn when headsProvider != nil AND headsProvider != provider; an identical heads provider collapses back to the single-provider layout
Role labels are the literal strings "Lead" and "Heads", joined to the display name with a spaced middle dot, e.g. "Lead · <Provider>"
The context block requires BOTH usage.fraction and usage.windowTokens non-nil (showsContext); the same pair also guards the if-let that draws it
A provider reporting neither limits nor credits gets no section at all, and the heads section's leading divider is suppressed when nothing preceded it
tokens(_:) thresholds: count >= 1_000_000_000 -> "B", >= 1_000_000 -> "M", >= 1_000 -> "k", otherwise the plain integer string
tokens(_:) formats one decimal with "%.1f" and strips a trailing ".0", so 1000 -> "1k", 1500 -> "1.5k", 1_200_000 -> "1.2M"
Context percentage is Int((fraction * 100).rounded()), so a tiny non-zero fraction still rounds to 0% below 0.005
Refresh happens once per appearance, for the lead and, when applicable, the heads provider
unresolved_questions: ContextUsage's declaration is outside this file; usage here implies usedTokens: Int, windowTokens: Int?, fraction: Double?
Whether refreshPlanLimits/refreshCredits are async, debounced or cached inside the registry is not visible here
compact() uses String(format:) so the decimal separator is locale-dependent; whether the app pins a locale cannot be determined from this file

files.purpose: The shared building blocks behind every usage readout: PlanLimitsView (plan-name header, a LimitRow per rolling window, banked resets, and the problem or login note), CreditsView (pay-as-you-go balance with a Top up link), the private BankedResetsView and BankedResetRow pair that spends a reset credit through the registry, and the UsageBar capsule used by all of them.
key_symbols: private func note(for credits: ProviderCredits?, isLoading: Bool) -> String? on CreditsView
private static func tint(for percent: Double) -> Color on LimitRow
static func resetText(_ date: Date, now: Date = .now) -> String on LimitRow
fileprivate struct BankedResetRowModel: Identifiable { var id: String; var credit: PlanLimits.ResetCredit? }
fileprivate enum BankedResetsView.Phase: Equatable with cases idle, confirming(String), applying(String), done(PlanLimits.ResetOutcome), failed(String)
struct UsageBar: View with let fraction: Double, let tint: Color, var label = "Used"
calls_into: Chrome.primaryText, Chrome.secondaryText, Chrome.accent, Chrome.warning, Chrome.danger, Chrome.success, Chrome.overlay(_:), Chrome.panelSlide
state_owned: PlanLimitsView: @Environment(AppModel.self) private var model; let provider: ProviderKind (no @State)
CreditsView: @Environment(AppModel.self) private var model; let provider: ProviderKind (no @State)

BankedResetsView: @Environment(AppModel.self) private var model; let provider: ProviderKind; let credits: PlanLimits.ResetCredits; @State private var phase: Phase = .idle; @State private var settle: Task<Void, Never>?
BankedResetRow: let row, index, several, phase plus onConfirm/onCancel/onUse closures, stateless
UsageBar: let fraction: Double; let tint: Color; var label = "Used"
side_effects: Workspace.openTerminal(running: provider.loginCommand) launches a terminal running the provider's login command when the "Login" button is pressed
Link("Top up", destination: topUpURL) opens the provider's dashboard top-up page
BankedResetsView.spend starts an unstructured Task that awaits model.providers.consumeResetCredit(provider, row.credit?.id), an app-server call that spends a banked reset
After the call the same Task sleeps with try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(4)) and then sets phase back to .idle unless cancelled
The previous settle Task is cancelled before a new spend and again on .onDisappear
No direct file writes, keychain access or notifications in this file
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI on macOS with the Observation @Environment(AppModel.self) form
buttonStyle(.glass) and buttonStyle(.glassProminent), the macOS 26 Liquid Glass button styles
Workspace.openTerminal implies a macOS terminal launch for the login flow
Swift Concurrency Task, Task.sleep(for:) and Task.isCancelled
persisted_fields: None persisted by these views. State is either in-memory registry data (planLimits, credits, loadingLimits, loadingCredits) or the transient @State phase, which returns to .idle after 4 seconds.
ui_elements: PlanLimitsView root: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0)

PlanLimitsView header: HStack(spacing: 8) with Text(verbatim: limits?.planName.map { "Plan usage limits · \($0)" } ?? "Plan usage limits") at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.secondaryText, Spacer(minLength: 8), and ProgressView().controlSize(.mini) while loading
Each LimitRow gets .padding(.top, 14)
Divider().padding(.top, 14) before BankedResetsView only when limits.windows is non-empty; BankedResetsView itself gets .padding(.top, 14)

API-key problem note: HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 6) with Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill") at .font(.system(size: 10, weight: .semibold)) in Chrome.warning, Text(verbatim: problem) at .font(.system(size: 11)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .lineLimit(2) and .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true), then Spacer(minLength: 8); whole row .padding(.top, 14)

Signed-in provider problem note: HStack(spacing: 8) with Text(verbatim: "Click here to login again") at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText, Spacer(minLength: 8), Button("Login") with .buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small); whole row .padding(.top, 14)
No-limits fallback: Text(verbatim: "\(provider.displayName) did not report plan limits.") at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .padding(.top, 8)
PlanLimitsView animation: .animation(Chrome.panelSlide, value: limits)

CreditsView row: HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 16); left VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) with Text(verbatim: "Remaining credits") at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.primaryText and the note at .font(.system(size: 11)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)

CreditsView right side: Spacer(minLength: 12) then HStack(spacing: 10) with ProgressView().controlSize(.mini) while loading, Text(verbatim: credits.amountText) at .font(.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) with .monospacedDigit() coloured Chrome.danger when isDepleted else Chrome.primaryText and .lineLimit(1), then Link("Top up", destination:) with .buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small)
CreditsView animation: .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: credits)

LimitRow: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8); top HStack(spacing: 12) with window.title at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.primaryText .lineLimit(1), Spacer(minLength: 8), optional Text(verbatim: "Resets \(Self.resetText(resetsAt))") at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText .lineLimit(1), and Text(verbatim: "\(Int(window.percent.rounded()))%") at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .monospacedDigit()
LimitRow detail line: .font(.system(size: 11)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .lineLimit(1)
LimitRow bar: UsageBar(fraction: window.percent / 100, tint: Self.tint(for: window.percent), label: window.title)

BankedResetsView header: HStack(spacing: 6) with Text(verbatim: "Banked resets") at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.primaryText and Text(verbatim: "· \(countText)") at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText with .contentTransition(.numericText()); .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) so VoiceOver reads it as one line, "Banked resets, 2 available"

Status line, done: HStack(spacing: 5) with Image(systemName: outcome == .reset ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "info.circle") at .font(.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)) tinted Chrome.success for .reset else Chrome.secondaryText, with .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: phase); Text(verbatim: outcome.message) at .font(.system(size: 11)) in the same tint; .padding(.top, 4); .transition(.blurReplace)
Status line, failed: Text(verbatim: message) at .font(.system(size: 11)) in Chrome.danger, .padding(.top, 4), .transition(.blurReplace)
Each BankedResetRow: .padding(.top, 12) and .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .move(edge: .top)))
BankedResetsView animations: .animation(Chrome.panelSlide, value: phase) and .animation(Chrome.panelSlide, value: credits)

BankedResetRow: HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 12); left VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) with the title at .font(.system(size: 13)) in Chrome.primaryText .lineLimit(1) and the detail or expiry at .font(.system(size: 11)) in Chrome.secondaryText .lineLimit(1); Spacer(minLength: 12); then the control

Confirm control: HStack(spacing: 6) with Button("Cancel").buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small) and Button("Reset now").buttonStyle(.glassProminent).controlSize(.small).tint(Chrome.accent); .transition(.blurReplace)

Applying control: HStack(spacing: 6) with ProgressView().controlSize(.mini) and Text(verbatim: "Resetting…") (U+2026 ellipsis) at .font(.system(size: 12)) in Chrome.secondaryText; .transition(.blurReplace)
Idle control: Button("Use reset").buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small) with .disabled(isApplying) and .transition(.blurReplace)

UsageBar: GeometryReader wrapping ZStack(alignment: .leading) of a background Capsule(style: .continuous).fill(Chrome.overlay(0.1)) and a foreground Capsule(style: .continuous).fill(tint); .frame(height: 5)
feature_notes: Plan header text is exactly "Plan usage limits" or "Plan usage limits · <planName>" with a spaced middle dot
LimitRow tint thresholds: percent >= 90 -> Chrome.danger, percent >= 75 -> Chrome.warning, otherwise Chrome.accent

resetText(_:now:): under 86_400 seconds it reads "in \(hours) hr \(minutes) min" when hours > 0, otherwise "in \(max(1, minutes)) min" so it never says "in 0 min"; under 6 * 86_400 seconds it uses the abbreviated weekday with hour and minute; beyond that the abbreviated month and day
resetText clamps a past date with max(0, date.timeIntervalSince(now))
The divider between the windows and the banked resets is suppressed when limits.windows is empty; the comment records that a plan with no resets to bank used to end on a line to nothing

The problem note branches on provider.isAPIKeyBased: API-key providers get a warning triangle and the provider's own message capped at 2 lines; signed-in providers get "Click here to login again" plus a "Login" button that runs provider.loginCommand in a terminal

Credits note logic: no credits and not loading -> "<Provider> did not report a balance."; no credits while loading -> no note at all; depleted -> "<Provider> declines turns until the balance is topped up."; otherwise credits.breakdownText, described as the top-up and grant split
The "Top up" Link only appears when CreditsReader.topUpURL(provider) returns a URL

Banked reset rows are the listed credits followed by placeholders for any unlisted balance: (0..<max(0, credits.availableCount - listed.count)) with ids "unlisted-0", "unlisted-1" and so on and a nil credit
A placeholder row's title is "Reset \(index + 1)" when rows.count > 1, otherwise plain "Reset"
expiryText: "No expiry reported" when no expiresAt, "Expired" when expiresAt <= .now, otherwise "Expires " + LimitRow.resetText(expiresAt)
countText: 0 -> "None available yet", 1 -> "1 available", otherwise "\(availableCount) available"
Spending a reset is a two-step confirmation: "Use reset" -> "Cancel" / "Reset now" -> spinner with "Resetting…" -> a status line held for 4 seconds -> back to .idle

Phase carries the row id, so only the row being confirmed or applied swaps its control; other rows keep "Use reset" but are disabled while any row is applying, because isApplying tests the whole phase
The settle Task is cancelled on .onDisappear so a dismissed panel cannot flip its phase afterwards

UsageBar fill width: max(fraction > 0 ? 5 : 0, proxy.size.width * min(max(fraction, 0), 1)), so a non-zero fraction always shows at least a 5 point nub and a zero fraction shows nothing; the bar is 5 points tall
UsageBar accessibility: .accessibilityElement() with label from the `label` property (default "Used") and value "\(Int((clamped * 100).rounded()))% used"
PlanLimitsView and CreditsView only render; refreshing is explicitly the caller's job per the file's doc comment, and UsagePanel is the caller that refreshes

provider.loginCommand's exact string and which terminal Workspace.openTerminal launches are not in this file
